title: Objective Tiling & Interteam Commitment Protocol
creator: Marcus Chen
description: Create a repeatable playbook and lightweight tooling to decompose company-level OKRs into non-overlapping 'tiles' owned by teams, plus an interteam commitment protocol for cross-functional handoffs during quarterly cycles. The goal is to reduce duplicated work, clarify ownership for shared outcomes, make dependencies explicit in roadmap planning, and provide a safety net (escalation + reserve lanes) for high-risk initiatives.
acceptance_criteria: Company-level OKRs are decomposed into tiled deliverables with an owner for each tile (pilot: Growth, Platform, Core Infra).
An interteam commitment protocol is documented and ratified by PM, Eng, and Design leads (includes intake template, handoff checklist, and escalation rules).
A dependency matrix (sheet + Console view) is populated and surfaced to senior PMs and Eng managers for the pilot teams.
Rollout plan and success metrics (on-time delivery, dependency resolution time, % of tiles delivered) are defined and instrumented in the Console dashboard.
Pilot run completed for one cycle and a retrospective with concrete changes for Q3 is delivered.

decisions: Use 'tiling' metaphor: non-overlapping, named tiles mapped to company OKRs to reduce duplicate work and surface ownership.
Pilot teams: Growth, Platform, Core Infra to validate cross-functional flows before wider rollout.
Dependency SLA: first response within 48 hours for pilot; escalate to Manager if not acknowledged within 72 hours.
Expose a minimal 'Tile Ledger' view in Console that shows owner, status, key dependencies, and last update timestamp.
